title: CEO Interview with Alex Higginbottom of Zenithon
gist: Zenithon, founded in July 2025 and just funded with $10 million, is building pretrained 'world models for extreme physics' that it says can search semiconductor process spaces (e.g. plasma etch, ~100 trillion recipe combinations) a million times faster than conventional solvers. The CEO frames the real competitors as incumbent trial-and-error methods and the poor track record of earlier ML in semiconductor process.

insights.claim: Zenithon argues that the most complex machines, such as plasma etch chambers, are still developed by build-test-fix cycles taking weeks or months because their internals cannot be observed or computed fast enough to search systematically.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Process-development cycle time is the bottleneck Zenithon targets; any tool that shortens it has direct value for fab and equipment R&D budgets.
insights.quote: The most complex machines ever built are still developed by trial and error.

insights.claim: A plasma etch recipe space contains on the order of 100 trillion possible combinations, which is why Zenithon says engineering advances only incrementally by experiment.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: The size of the search space is the core justification for ML-driven search over experiments.
insights.quote: under recipes with on the order of 100 trillion possible combinations

insights.claim: Process engineers' underlying anxiety is that the search space has grown faster than tools can handle, while the veterans whose intuition guided recipe design are retiring.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Retiring expertise plus rising dimensionality creates demand for automated process optimization in fabs.
insights.quote: the people who spent careers building that intuition are retiring
insights.locator: What keeps your customers up at night?

insights.claim: Zenithon claims its world models can explore a million design points in the time a conventional solver runs one, and search semiconductor process spaces a million times faster to produce better designs.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Vendor claim with no independent benchmark given; watch for pilot results and named customers.
insights.quote: We’re building models to explore a million design points in the time a conventional solver takes to run one.

insights.claim: Zenithon says its strongest application areas are semiconductor processes, particularly plasma etching, deposition, and reactor design and optimization.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Initial wedge is semiconductor equipment and process R&D, a market tied to fab capex.
insights.quote: Semiconductor processes, particularly plasma etching, deposition, and reactor design and optimization.
insights.locator: What application areas are your strongest?

insights.claim: Zenithon says it has raised $10 million and was started in July 2025 by Alex Higginbottom and Abetharan Antony.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Early-stage funding scale signals a seed-sized bet on AI-for-physics in semiconductor tooling.
insights.quote: have just raised $10 million to accelerate our development of world models

themes.theme: Competition and the ML track record

insights.claim: Zenithon says its biggest competitor is the existing method: engineers choose between it and running another simulation, not between it and another AI model.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Adoption hurdle is workflow inertia, so pilots and integration with existing simulators matter more than model rivalry.
insights.quote: The thing we compete with most is the existing method.
insights.locator: What does the competitive landscape look like

insights.claim: Earlier machine learning in semiconductor process mostly disappointed because each problem needed its own dataset, data generation was slow, and any design change made the model worthless.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Explains why prior ML-for-process vendors struggled; a new entrant must show generalization across designs.
insights.quote: Machine learning has been applied to semiconductor process before and mostly disappointed.
insights.locator: The harder competitor is the track record.

insights.claim: Zenithon's answer is models pretrained across problems rather than fitted to one, plus an in-house data generation layer because no public corpus for this physics exists; the CEO says it must be shown rather than asserted.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Proprietary data generation could be a moat but is unproven; look for demonstrated cross-regime transfer.
insights.quote: Whether it holds is something we intend to show rather than assert.
insights.locator: Our answer is that our models are pretrained

insights.claim: Zenithon plans a new model generation roughly every three months, with about half of its raise going to compute and half to headcount.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Compute-heavy spend and quarterly cadence imply the $10 million runway is short, raising follow-on funding risk.
insights.quote: We’re aiming to ship a new model generation roughly every three months
insights.locator: What new features and technology are you working on?

insights.claim: Zenithon aims to train directly from experimental output rather than simulation alone, which it says closes the sim-real gap, and to scale one product across many physical regimes instead of bespoke models per problem.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Training on real experimental data is the key technical differentiator to monitor.
insights.quote: which closes the sim-real gap rather than widening it
insights.locator: What new features and technology are you working on?

insights.claim: Customers engage by booking demos on Zenithon's website, starting with a pilot and then optionally a custom deal for support and a full world model fine-tuned to their system.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Pilot-to-custom-deal structure indicates a services-heavy early revenue model.
insights.quote: Customers book demos with us through our website.
insights.locator: How do customers normally engage with your company?
